chunks: Aban ibn Uthman from Isa ibn Abdillah al-Qummi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Three people's supplication is answered: one of them is the warrior (mujahid) in the path of Allah, so see how you leave him (in his absence).

key_terms.الْغَازِي: The warrior or mujahid striving in the path of God

ai.seo_question: Who are the three people whose prayers are always answered according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to underscore the spiritual merit of the *ghazi* (warrior), linking their accepted supplication to the community's duty of maintaining their affairs and family during absence. This highlights the socio-spiritual dimension of Jihad in Shia jurisprudence, where communal support ensures the warrior's focus remains on divine striving. The emphasis on 'how you leave him' reflects the broader Islamic principle of caring for those engaged in obligatory or voluntary acts of worship.
